payload.statement: A homogeneous steady state of two reacting chemicals that is stable without diffusion can become unstable to spatial perturbations when the chemicals diffuse at different rates, spontaneously producing a pattern.
payload.title: Turing diffusion-driven instability

assumptions: Declared linearization J=[[1,-2],[2,-3]], Du=1, Dv=10: a worked instance, not fitted to any data.
Two species, linear stability about a homogeneous steady state, 1-D interval, zero-flux boundaries.
Neumann mode numbers are DEFINED as q_n=(n*pi/L)^2; they are not derived from the boundary-value problem in this run.
A mode is stable iff trace<0 and det>0 (Routh-Hurwitz for a 2x2 matrix); modes n=0..100 are scanned.
payload.context: Applicability witness for the Delphi claim turing-ddi. For J=[[1,-2],[2,-3]], Du=1, Dv=10 the continuum inequality Dv*fu+Du*gv > 2*sqrt(Du*Dv*detJ) holds (49 > 40), yet every admissible Neumann mode is stable on L=pi and L=5pi/2, while a non-stable mode exists on 3pi/2, 2pi, 3pi and 4pi. It shows the admissible-mode set decides the outcome; it does not support the claim's headline and carries no stance field because the Evidence schema has none.

payload.method: Exact-rational scan. For each domain length L=(p/s)*pi in {pi, 3pi/2, 2pi, 5pi/2, 3pi, 4pi} form the Neumann mode numbers q_n=(n*s/p)^2, n=0..100, and compute trace=(a+d)-(Du+Dv)q and det=(Du*q-a)*(Dv*q-d)-b*c with Python Fractions. A mode is non-stable unless trace<0 and det>0. Executed as `python3 run_modes.py` on the OpenResearch local backend.
